title: Reconcile QA role doc with moe-qa-loop skill on waiting for the completion commit
description: docs/roles/qa.md line 8 tells QA 'Do NOT wait' for task.commits and to stage/land the row's own paths itself, while docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md step 3 says an empty task.commits 'means the evidence is not yet verifiable ... wait for it before reviewing' and never review the dirty shared tree. Agents load both, so QA behaviour is currently whichever text it read last. Pick ONE rule and make both documents state it. Recommended interim rule until the Wave 1 finalize/candidate work lands: wait a bounded time (e.g. poll get_context for task.commits up to ~2 minutes) because the wrapper lands seconds after REVIEW; only if nothing arrives, fall back to the role doc's measured-attribution self-landing procedure, and say so in the qa_approve summary. Keep docs/roles/qa.md under the 40-line lint cap; put the long procedure in qa.reference.md. Role docs reach IDE users only via daemon prebuild + plugin rebuild, so also regenerate packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts (npm run build). Source: roadmap 2026-09-10 §2.
definitionOfDone: docs/roles/qa.md and docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md give the same instruction for an empty task.commits, including the bounded wait and the fallback
npm run lint (role-doc linter) passes with qa.md at or under 40 lines
A daemon test or doc test asserts the two documents do not contain the contradictory phrases ('Do NOT wait' vs 'wait for it before reviewing') — or an equivalent guard
Rationale recorded in docs/roles/qa.reference.md pointing at the 2026-09-06 measurement (one completion in three reached REVIEW with bytes only in the dirty tree)

Define two shared constants at the top of the file:
  const FORBIDDEN = ['Do NOT wait', 'wait for it before reviewing'];
  const SENTINELS = ['bounded wait, not a blocker', 'up to ~2 minutes', 'land it yourself', 'record_commit'];

Subjects under test — four texts:
  a) ROLE_DOCS['qa.md']
  b) SKILL_FILES['moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md']
  c) the same two files read from disk at `path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..', '..', '..', 'docs', ...)` (src/util -> src -> moe-daemon -> packages -> repo root), LF-normalized with `.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n')` before any comparison.

Assertions:
  1. For each of the four texts: every FORBIDDEN literal is absent. Use an explicit per-phrase assertion so the failure message names the offending phrase and file, e.g. `expect(text, `${label} still carries "${phrase}"`).not.toContain(phrase)`.
  2. For each of the four texts: every SENTINEL is present. This positive half is what fails if a future edit deletes the rule instead of restating it, and what fails if a generated file is stale (the generated copy would still hold the old text).
  3. ROLE_DOCS['qa.reference.md'] contains '2026-09-06' and 'one completion in three' (DoD item 5's rationale anchor).
  4. Both generated keys exist and are non-empty — this is the error handling that stops a renamed skill directory or a dropped ROLE_DOCS key from silently turning every other assertion into a vacuous pass on `undefined`. Assert presence explicitly before reading the text, so the failure says 'key missing' instead of throwing a bare TypeError.

implementationPlan.description:
Write the canonical rule into `docs/roles/qa.md` and move the long procedure plus its rationale into `docs/roles/qa.reference.md`.

In qa.md, replace the whole of line 8 (the `Audit task.commits` bullet) with ONE bullet — keep the file's one-long-bullet-per-rule style so the line count barely moves:

- Audit `task.commits` from `get_context` — review the recorded completion commit (`git show <sha>`, `git branch --contains <sha>`), never the dirty shared tree. An empty `task.commits` at REVIEW is a bounded wait, not a blocker: re-run `task.verification` and the tests first, then re-poll `get_context` — up to ~2 minutes total, because the wrapper lands seconds after REVIEW. If a completion commit arrives, review that. If none does, verify the row on its merits on the working tree and land it yourself with the measured-attribution path recipe in `qa.reference.md` — then `moe.record_commit`, then approve, saying in the `qa_approve` summary that you self-landed after the bounded wait expired. A `NO-COMPLETION-COMMIT` warning after that is a daemon race, not a defect.

That bullet carries all four sentinels the guard test looks for and drops the phrase 'Do NOT wait'. Do not reintroduce that literal anywhere in the file.

In qa.reference.md, add a new section after 'Review order (do not skip)' titled `## Empty \`task.commits\` at REVIEW`. It holds three things:
  1. The rule restated in full (bounded wait, then fallback, then record_commit, then say so in the approve summary).
  2. The measured-attribution path recipe MOVED VERBATIM out of qa.md — the per-path `git diff -- <path> | grep '^[+-]' | grep -v '^[+-][+-]' | grep -vi '<row vocabulary>'` must-be-EMPTY check, the rule that a path also carrying a peer's hunks is EXCLUDED WHOLE because the peer's own landing carries it, that partial-hunk staging is a last resort needing a bare commit, and the task trailer + `moe.record_commit` finish. Do not reword or 'improve' this recipe — the governor ruling keeps it canonical.
  3. Rationale: measured 2026-09-06, one completion in three reached REVIEW with its bytes only in the dirty tree, because a wrapper lands a row only when its CLI process exits on that row — a session that hopped to another row, or an interactive seat that never exits, can never fire it. Record that `docs/roles/qa.md` (269d3fe, 2026-09-06) supersedes `docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md` (bf3f8fa, 2026-08-29) per the governor ruling, and that this is the interim rule until the Wave 1 finalize/candidate work lands.

Also reconcile the third statement of the same policy: item 3 of 'Review order (do not skip)' currently says 'Fall back to the working tree only when no commit exists, and then expect — and act on — the `qa_approve` `NO-COMPLETION-COMMIT` warning.' Replace that sentence with a pointer to the new section so the reference doc does not contradict itself.

qa.reference.md is exempt from the 40-line cap; qa.md is not. Run `npm run lint` from the repo root (Git Bash) or `scripts/lint-role-docs.ps1` and confirm qa.md is at or under 40 lines.

implementationPlan.description:
Reconcile `docs/skills/moe-qa-loop/SKILL.md` to the same rule. Six edits, all in that one file.

1. Step 3 of 'The decision flow' (line 18): delete the sentence 'An empty `task.commits` means the evidence is not yet verifiable: the wrapper lands the commit seconds after REVIEW, so wait for it before reviewing.' Replace it with the same rule qa.md now states, using the SAME four sentinel phrases verbatim ('bounded wait, not a blocker', 'up to ~2 minutes', 'land it yourself', `moe.record_commit`), and point at `.moe/roles/qa.reference.md` for the path-scoping recipe. Keep 'Do not review the dirty shared working tree — other sessions' edits live there too' as the rule for the normal case, but make it explicit that the self-landing fallback is the one sanctioned exception and that it is scoped to paths measured to be this row's own.

2. Make the ordering carry the wait: step 2 already re-runs `task.verification`, so state in step 3 that the re-poll happens after that re-run rather than as an idle sleep. Do not introduce a sleep loop.

3. 'Approve when' (line 40): change 'task.commits contains a completion commit recorded for this review round and reachable from the shared branch' to also accept the commit QA landed itself after the bounded wait expired.

4. 'Reject when' (line 51): this bullet currently rejects whenever no completion commit exists and the landing had time to run. That is now wrong — the fallback is to land it, not to reject. Narrow it to the case where the bytes genuinely are not there or cannot be attributed: no owned paths, or every dirty path also carries a peer's hunks so the whole-path exclusion leaves nothing to land. Keep the existing `lastCommitOutcome` refused/failed signal as evidence for that case. This bullet is the error handling for a fallback that legitimately cannot run — without it the reconciled flow would have no defined exit when self-landing refuses.

5. The approve paragraph (line 46) says a `NO-COMPLETION-COMMIT` warning is 'expected only with autoCommit off or when you approved inside the post-flight race; otherwise you should have rejected'. Change the tail to 'otherwise you should have landed it yourself first'.

6. Frontmatter `allowed-tools`: the skill currently permits only read-only git (`git diff`, `git log`, `git show`, `git branch`), which makes the canonical fallback unexecutable from inside the skill. Add the minimum needed to run the recipe: `Bash(git add:*)`, `Bash(git commit:*)`, `Bash(git status:*)`, `Bash(git rev-parse:*)`. Add nothing broader — no bare `Bash(git:*)`, no push.

Do not touch the oversized-diff, review-depth, reject-quality, or 'what never to do' sections — they are out of scope.

The recipe's commands (`git diff`, `git status`, `git add`, `git commit`) are now all permitted, so the canonical fallback is executable from inside the skill.

Regression green, adversarial pass done, two real findings acted on.

**Regression.** `npm test` from packages/moe-daemon, fresh after every edit: **`Test Files 103 passed (103) | Tests 1183 passed (1183)`**, exit 0, 7.5s. No failures, so nothing to classify as pre-existing vs regression. `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0. `npm run lint` from repo root exit 0 — "OK: docs/roles/qa.md has 25 lines (max 40)". **Adversarial answers, one by one.**

1. *Do all four texts give the same instruction?* Yes — verified by loading the generated constants with tsx and printing the policy region of all four side by side, not by trusting the phrase guard. Source and generated are character-identical for both docs. qa.md and SKILL.md word it differently but instruct identically: bounded wait of up to ~2 minutes absorbed by the verification/test re-run, re-poll `get_context`, commit arrives -> review that, none -> self-land the row's measured paths -> `moe.record_commit` -> approve saying you self-landed.

2. *Any doc still contradicting where the guard does not look?* qa.reference.md "Review order" item 3 now points at the new section instead of the old fall-back-and-expect-the-warning sentence. The SKILL's Approve-when, Reject-when and approve paragraph all restate the new rule. **But a FOURTH statement existed outside the three planned docs**: `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md:659` said "Policy for QA: treat the warning as a reject unless you verified HEAD yourself". That is the exact defect this task exists to kill, one grep away from any QA seat. **Scope grown by one paragraph, deliberately** — replaced with a pointer to qa.md / qa.reference.md plus "a warning that fires after QA landed the row itself and called `moe.record_commit` is this race, not a defect; it is grounds to reject only when the bytes cannot be attributed to the row at all", keeping the true tail "a DONE task with no completion commit from anyone is still a merge with no reviewed diff". Verified TROUBLESHOOTING.md is NOT vendored (the generators read only docs/roles, docs/agents, docs/skills), so no regeneration was needed for it. Also checked `docs/roles/governor.md:42` and `governor.reference.md:95` — they describe governor triage of the post-hoc alert, not QA behaviour at REVIEW, and stay true after a QA self-land (there IS a completion commit then). Left alone.

3. *Is the fallback executable as written?* Every **git** command the recipe names was covered by the four added entries — but the recipe is a pipeline, `git diff -- <path> | grep '^[+-]' | grep -v ... | grep -vi ...`, and `grep` had no Bash permission of its own, so a QA seat would stall on the very check that decides which paths are safe to stage. **Added `Bash(grep:*)` — one entry beyond the four the step enumerated.** Justification: read-only, strictly narrower than the `Bash(git:*)` the step forbade, and without it the canonical fallback is still unexecutable, which was the whole point of edit 6. skillFiles.ts regenerated afterwards; all suites re-run green.

4. *Defined exit for every path?* Commit arrives during the wait -> "review that" (both docs).
